rationale: The reviewer identified the random pair split that leaves every test protein in training, and showed that a per-protein training interaction-rate baseline matches the model (100% of test proteins seen in training; baseline AUROC 0.795 vs 0.790). They proposed held-out-protein splits plus a degree baseline. Their other points (homolog clustering, negative-selection bias, small sample) are refinements or generic caveats rather than distinct demonstrated problems.
